subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a Christian wedding, what is the significance of the vows being made 'till death us do part'?
options: They express the intention that marriage is a lifelong commitment
They mean the couple may separate after one year
They are a legal formality with no religious meaning
They apply only if children are born
questions.explain: The phrase shows that marriage is intended as a permanent, lifelong bond between the couple.

questions.q: What does a Humanist typically believe about same-sex marriage?
options: It is only valid if blessed by a priest
It should be banned in all circumstances
It is wrong because it is unnatural
It is acceptable, as love and commitment matter more than gender
questions.explain: Humanists generally support same-sex marriage, valuing loving commitment regardless of the partners' gender.

questions.q: Which view best describes a liberal Christian attitude to remarriage after divorce?
options: Divorced people must leave the faith
Remarriage may be permitted as God offers forgiveness and new beginnings
Marriage is never a serious commitment
Remarriage is forbidden in all circumstances
questions.explain: Some Christians believe forgiveness and compassion allow for remarriage after divorce.

questions.q: What is one religious argument sometimes given in support of traditional gender roles in the family?
options: That such roles are based on certain scriptural teachings about complementary responsibilities
That men should not work
That children should raise themselves
That women are not human
questions.explain: Some believers cite scripture to support distinct but complementary roles, though others interpret these texts differently.

questions.q: Which is a reason some couples give for choosing to cohabit rather than marry?
options: Marriage is illegal in the UK
Cohabitation guarantees children
They want to test their compatibility before any lifelong commitment
Cohabitation is required by religious law
questions.explain: Some couples cohabit to test their relationship or because they do not see marriage as necessary, though some faiths discourage this.

questions.q: Which statement best reflects Roman Catholic teaching on divorce?
options: Divorce is encouraged whenever a couple is unhappy
Remarriage in church is automatically granted to all
Marriage vows are considered temporary
The Church does not recognise the dissolution of a valid sacramental marriage
questions.explain: The Catholic Church teaches marriage is a lifelong sacrament and does not recognise divorce as ending a valid marriage.

questions.q: What is 'cohabitation'?
options: A vow of lifelong celibacy
Living together as a couple without being married
A form of religious pilgrimage
A religious ceremony of marriage
questions.explain: Cohabitation means a couple living together in a sexual relationship without being legally married.

questions.q: According to traditional Christian teaching, what is one of the main purposes of marriage?
options: To gain financial advantage over others
To provide a stable, loving union for procreation and mutual support
To remove the need for religious commitment
To guarantee a couple will never face difficulty
questions.explain: Many Christian traditions teach that marriage is for lifelong companionship, mutual support and the raising of children.

questions.q: Which of the following is commonly described as a purpose of the family in religious teaching?
options: To replace the need for community
To avoid all responsibility for others
To bring up children and pass on faith and values
To isolate members from wider society
questions.explain: Many faiths see the family as the place where children are nurtured and religious and moral values are passed on.

questions.q: What does 'celibacy' mean in a religious context?
options: Marrying as young as possible
Rejecting all religious belief
Having many marriages
Abstaining from marriage and sexual relations, often for religious devotion
questions.explain: Celibacy is the choice to abstain from marriage and sexual activity, often to focus on religious service.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a secular (non-religious) view of marriage often held in the UK today?
options: Marriage is one valid option, and cohabitation or civil partnership are equally acceptable
Only religious people may marry
Marriage must always be arranged
Marriage is forbidden by law
questions.explain: Many non-religious people see marriage as one of several equally valid ways to form a committed relationship.

questions.q: Which view on contraception is held by the Roman Catholic Church?
options: All forms of contraception are strongly encouraged
Contraception is compulsory for married couples
The Church has no teaching on the subject
Artificial contraception is generally opposed, with natural family planning permitted
questions.explain: Catholic teaching generally opposes artificial contraception while permitting natural methods of family planning.

questions.q: Which of these would many religious believers see as a benefit of contraception within marriage?
options: It guarantees a happy marriage
It is required before every marriage
It allows couples to plan their family responsibly
It removes the need for love
questions.explain: Many believers, especially in liberal traditions, accept contraception as a way to plan a family responsibly.

questions.q: What is 'adultery'?
options: Choosing not to marry for religious reasons
A wedding ceremony in a register office
Marrying more than one person at once
A married person having a sexual relationship with someone other than their spouse
questions.explain: Adultery is sexual unfaithfulness by a married person, condemned by many religious traditions.

questions.q: Which term describes a marriage in which the partners are chosen by their families, with the couple's consent?
options: An annulment
A forced marriage
An arranged marriage
A civil partnership
questions.explain: An arranged marriage involves families helping to choose partners, but with the couple's free consent, unlike a forced marriage.

questions.q: What do most traditional religious teachings say about sexual relationships?
options: They are required of everyone before marriage
They should only take place within marriage
They are forbidden under all circumstances
They have no moral dimension at all
questions.explain: Many religious traditions teach that sex is best expressed within the commitment of marriage.

questions.q: Why do some Christians believe procreation is an important purpose of sex?
options: Because it removes the need for marriage
Because the law requires every couple to have children
Because the Bible includes the command to 'be fruitful and multiply'
Because it is the only purpose sex can have
questions.explain: The Genesis command to 'be fruitful and multiply' is often cited to support procreation as a purpose of sex.

questions.q: What is a common misconception about religious views on same-sex relationships?
options: That all religious people hold exactly the same view
That some accept and some reject such relationships
That a range of views exists across and within faiths
That denominations can differ on this issue
questions.explain: The misconception is believing all religious people hold exactly the same view; in reality attitudes to same-sex relationships vary widely both within and between religions.

questions.q: What is 'polygamy'?
options: Choosing lifelong celibacy
Living together without marriage
Being married to more than one person at the same time
Marrying within the same family
questions.explain: Polygamy is the practice of having more than one spouse at the same time, accepted in some cultures but not in UK law.

questions.q: Which statement best reflects the view of Christians who fully support women being ordained as priests or ministers?
options: Leadership should be based on calling and gifts, not gender
Women cannot serve God in any role
Only men were created in God's image
Worship should exclude women entirely
questions.explain: Many Christians argue that women and men are equally called to leadership, based on gifts rather than gender.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a view supporting gender equality found in many modern religious communities?
options: Men and women have equal value and dignity before God
Only men can possess a soul
Gender roles can never change
Women should never take part in worship
questions.explain: Many believers hold that, while roles may differ, men and women are of equal worth and dignity.

questions.q: Which religious group is well known for clergy taking vows of celibacy?
options: Roman Catholic priests
All Protestant ministers
All Jewish rabbis
All Muslim imams
questions.explain: Roman Catholic priests typically take vows of celibacy, unlike clergy in many other traditions who may marry.
